summary: Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday ran Iraqi football and its Olympic committee from 1984 until 2003, having players jailed, whipped and tortured in prison camps and red rooms after losses, while FIFA looked away.

evidence.note: birth in 1964 given, with two competing birth dates
Saddam hands him the Olympic committee and football federation at age twenty
Iraq's matches at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico reviewed in some detail
host argues Saddam abused the boy by exposing him to torture and executions
rape and abduction allegations, including a bride who killed herself afterwards
Latif Yahia's body-double claims and unchecked defector stories in Western press
red rooms in state sports facilities used to punish players
team captain held two weeks in a prison camp and flogged with cables
segment on coach Ammo Baba resisting Uday and being beaten in a stadium
FIFA investigates the 1997 abuse reports and finds nothing
killed by US forces in 2003; story ends there

notes: Story deliberately limits itself to Uday's football career; his other crimes are covered only briefly. Main span starts at his appointment at age twenty (about 1984, estimated). The 1960s team history and the 2026 World Cup are background and coda only. Child-abuse is secondary because the host spends several minutes framing Saddam's treatment of the young Uday as abuse.
